PullRequest.Title: Support presentation preferences for Markdown embedded editors
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
Expose generic presentation preferences for contributed Markdown code-block editors and consume their published runtime implementation.

- Accept and validate resizable, fullWidth, fullView, and minHeight in static contributions and exported provider results.
- Forward preferences through the Markdown editor RPC descriptor and include them in descriptor equality checks.
- Preserve contribution defaults when a resolved preference is undefined, while retaining explicit false overrides.
- Upgrade @vscode/markdown-editor from 0.0.2-121 to the published 0.0.2-130 release, including its registry lockfile integrity.
- Document the contract and add contribution/RPC schema and preference-merging regression tests.

Companion package implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/366 (merged and published). The publication blocker is resolved; no local dependency link is committed. This is generic extension integration and contains no Team Tools or VS Code Apps implementation.

## Validation
Validated against a worktree-local npm installation of @vscode/markdown-editor@0.0.2-130 (not the development checkout):
- 12 presentation/schema and generated-manifest tests passed.
- Markdown editor webview build passed.
- Markdown editor and extension TypeScript checks passed.
- Generated manifest check: unchanged.
- Targeted ESLint and precommit hygiene passed.

The previous Windows / Electron-Unit run had 25,079 passing tests and one unrelated teardown failure: session-storage compatibility cleanup received EBUSY unlinking agent-host.db. A new CI run is triggered by the dependency/fix commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the Markdown extension and discover contributed code-block editor providers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension activation imports contribution discovery and constructs Markdown contributions before starting the language client. The diff adds a bounded Zod validation of an optional four-field object for each contributed provider; MarkdownEditorProvider and its RPC protocol were already statically imported through extension.shared, so protocol construction was already on this activation path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of installed extensions contributing markdown.codeBlockEditorProviders and providers in their manifests; effective cardinality is one validation per declared provider during contribution refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous manifest iteration; no new queue, limiter, or asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Contributions are materialized and retained by the existing MarkdownContributionProvider, then recomputed on extension changes. No cache key, hit/miss behavior, or invalidation policy changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the execution path and O(provider-count) CPU scaling; high confidence that the incremental work is bounded and non-reportable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact installed provider count varies, but the added work is a fixed four-property schema check per provider and does not establish meaningful startup degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds only small in-process validation and stored metadata, without newly loading the RPC protocol or introducing an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Markdown custom editor with static embedded code-block editor providers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor open configures the webview immediately while #loadCodeBlockEditorProviders sequentially reads each existing static provider resource; provider definitions are published when ready. The diff only attaches the already parsed presentation object to each descriptor and compares four scalar fields on refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and decode the static provider HTML resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per static provider per Markdown editor open or qualifying provider refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resource was read and decoded once for every static provider on the same paths; the diff only adds presentation metadata to the resulting descriptor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider availability waits for these reads, but base webview configuration/rendering is initiated independently and this boundary predates the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish provider definitions from the extension host to the Markdown webview
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notification containing the grouped provider array on readiness or a material provider refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped notification carried provider descriptors; the diff adds a bounded optional object and does not increase notification count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Embedded provider selection depends on this notification; the added payload is at most four scalar fields per opted-in provider.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of static code-block editor providers, effectively one existing filesystem read per static provider per opened Markdown editor; presentation metadata adds constant-size serialization per provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Static provider resources remain read sequentially in the existing for/await loop. The diff neither increases cardinality nor changes scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static descriptors are loaded on each editor open as before and refreshed on contribution/resource changes. Equality now includes presentation fields so unchanged definitions remain suppressed; no positive or negative cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the open/update call flow and descriptor equality implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider HTML size and provider count vary, but neither filesystem cardinality nor concurrency changes; metadata overhead is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Existing I/O and grouped IPC behavior are unchanged, and the added comparison prevents presentation-only changes from being missed without causing repeated rebuilds for equal values.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve and instantiate a dynamic embedded editor for a matching fenced code block
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The webview requests a provider descriptor on first matching use. The extension may activate the provider extension, invoke resolve, optionally read a returned URI, validate the result, merge contribution and resolved presentation preferences, and return it over RPC before iframe instantiation. Only validation/merge and four optional scalars are added by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the contributing extension and call its exported resolve provider API
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one provider activation per contribution cache entry and one coalesced resolution per unique contribution/document/language until invalidation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extension activation and resolve call occurred with identical coalescing and timeout behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A matching embedded editor waits for provider resolution; this boundary and placement predate the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and decode provider HTML when resolve returns a URI
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read per cold coalesced resolution whose result uses a URI; inline HTML causes zero reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same URI result caused the same read and decode before descriptor return.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Iframe descriptor return waits for the read; the diff does not add or move it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and return the resolved code-block editor descriptor between webview and extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per cold webview provider/language resolution, with extension-side coalescing across identical request keys
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC request/response carried the descriptor without presentation preferences.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The matching embedded editor waits for the response; presentation adds only a constant-size optional field.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique contribution/document/language tuples after the existing promise cache and optional provider cacheKey aliasing; repeated matching blocks share the cached resolution for that tuple.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent requests for the same requestCacheKey coalesce on one promise. Different providers/documents/languages may resolve concurrently as before; the diff adds no burst or limiter change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful resolutions remain cached by contribution/document/language and optionally cacheKey; failures and undefined results are removed for retry. Presentation metadata is part of the cached descriptor and does not alter invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the request handler, promise cache, resolver, and resource-read call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-defined resolve duration and HTML size vary, but the diff does not affect their number, concurrency, or placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The only incremental work is fixed-size validation, at most one small merge allocation per cold resolution, and bounded serialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use resizable, full-width, or full-view presentation controls in an embedded editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An opted-in descriptor reaches the published @vscode/markdown-editor runtime, which owns user-triggered sizing and view-mode UI. The repository diff supplies preferences and updates the package version; no changed repository code performs per-frame geometry reads, scroll work, or repeated layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of instantiated opted-in embedded editors and explicit user interactions with their controls; preferences are four scalars per descriptor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Instantiation and UI interaction scheduling remain owned by the existing virtualized iframe factory/runtime; no changed host-side concurrency mechanism is present.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved descriptors, including preferences, use the existing resolution cache. No additional cache or invalidation loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the host integration is bounded; insufficient evidence of any pathological runtime layout mechanism in the supplied diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The dependency implementation is consumed as a published package and its internal layout cost is not exposed in this repository diff; there is no concrete evidence of forced synchronous layout or repeated reconstruction to support a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The presentation behavior is intentional and opt-in, and the supplied change does not prove a synchronous UI-work regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and traced activation, editor open/provider loading, dynamic resolution, RPC transport, caching, refresh, and presentation interaction paths. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was established, and the PR does not itself prove a shipped regression fix requiring blame.
